verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes smooth, controlled beverage flow as a persistent plumbing acceptance condition.
The client adds the concrete flow-rate constraint that dispensing must avoid both slow dripping and an explosive pour.
The client requires the dispensing design to preserve the drink's consistency and frothiness.
The acceptance resolves the immediately preceding proposal to fabricate rendering-like stainless-steel spouts, not the earlier froth-preservation method attributed to this Event.

value_updates.flow_continuity: clean, controlled, and seamless during pouring

verdicts.decision_note: The client sets concrete dispensing-flow acceptance conditions of a seamless controlled pour without sputtering; the solenoid sequence belongs to the separate dispensing-control Requirement.
The source explicitly changes downward spout orientation, which is owned by the narrower spout-geometry Requirement rather than dispensing-flow quality.

missing_event_candidates.description: The client confirms the solenoid approach and the mix-to-valve-opening-to-pour control sequence.
The client requires the spouts to pour downward as shown in the rendering rather than along a flat slope.
